newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called lower with cooler weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called lower with cooler weather.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open slightly lower Tuesday amid continuing cooler-than-normal weather across most of the U.S., industry sources said.
September over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.34 to $2.36 after settling to the upside Monday at $2.374 per million British thermal units.
On ACCESS, September last traded 0.9 cent lower at $2.365 after dipping to a low of $2.30.
Early Tuesday cash prices followed futures higher to about $2.29-2.34 at Henry Hub, traders said.

Technically, September support was pegged at $2.20 and then at $2.15-2.16 and along the short-term up trendline at $2.12. Resistance was seen at the new contract high of $2.385, with further selling likely at the May 7 spot continuation high of $2.43.
In Monday's cash, Gulf Coast prices firmed one to three cents to the mid-$2.20s at Henry Hub. Midcon pipes also were up slightly at $2.15-2.16.
Separately, injection estimates for Wednesday's American Gas Association's storage report are about 68 bcf.
